plan: [Third-price, 5 bidders: winner pays the 3rd-highest bid. With no past rounds and independent uniform values, I avoid risky overbidding that can cause negative payoff. Bidding my true value ($31) keeps me from ever paying more than my value while giving positive expected profit when the third-highest bid (determined by others) is below 31. This is a simple, robust best response under uncertainty for a one-shot game. ]

[Assume others bid their private values (0–49). If I guarantee winning, I will pay the third-highest among the four others; its expected value is 0.6*49 = 29.4, so my expected profit when always winning is 37 - 29.4 = 7.6. Bidding aggressively increases win probability and thus expected profit versus truthful bidding. I will place a clearly dominant high bid (well above 49) to secure the win under typical opponent behavior while accepting small risk if opponents irrationally overbid far above values.]

[This is a third-price auction: if I win I pay the second-highest among the four opponents. Overbidding can capture rare cases where the second-highest < my value but the highest > my value, but those cases are infrequent under uniform draws and overbidding risks negative payoff. With no history, the safe long-run profit-maximizing approach is to bid my true private value to avoid guaranteed losses from aggressive overbids.]

[Third-price auction: my bid mainly changes win probability, not the payment if I win. With value $45, it's optimal to bid aggressively because the chance that three others outbid me (so the third-price exceeds $45) is extremely small (~0.2%). If others bid their values, the expected third-highest ≈ $19.6, so securing the win yields large expected surplus (~$25). I'll place a high bid to almost certainly win while accepting the tiny risk of overpaying.]

[No prior history. With 5 bidders, if I win I pay the second-highest of the other four. Approximating others' bids as their values, P(win with bid B) ≈(B/49)^4 and expected payment given win ≈(3/5)B. Expected profit ≈(B/49)^4*(v - 0.6B). For v=8 this expression is maximized near B = 32/3 ≈10.67. To respect $0.1 increments and balance win chance vs payment risk, bid 10.7.]
